evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Legislature of the state of Utah:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Utah's personal identity abuse statute to reach AI-generated or simulated likenesses, voices and personas. Bars using an individual's personal identity in advertising, fundraising or solicitation without consent, and knowingly distributing tools whose primary purpose is unauthorized creation of such content; gives individuals civil remedies. Effective May 7, 2025.
summary.long: Amends Utah's personal identity abuse provisions (Sections 45-3-2 to 45-3-7). Section 45-3-2 defines advertisement, consent, content, generative artificial intelligence, personal identity (including simulations or recreations made by generative AI, computer animation or digital manipulation), publish and voice. Section 45-3-3 makes personal identity abused when content containing it is used to advertise products or services, fundraise, solicit donations or promote purchases, where it expresses or implies endorsement, creates confusion about participation, or creates a false impression, and consent has not been obtained. It also prohibits knowingly distributing, selling or licensing technology whose intended primary purpose is unauthorized creation or modification of such content for commercial purposes. Consent cannot be inferred from failure to object. Individuals may sue the person who caused publication for injunctive relief, damages, exemplary damages and attorney fees (45-3-4). Publishers may be sued if the content on its face signals non-consent and the publisher took no reasonable steps to assure consent (45-3-5). Section 45-3-7 exempts news, public affairs, entertainment, parody and similar works, and excludes interactive computer services for content provided by others. Prosecution under Section 76-9-407 is preserved. The act takes effect May 7, 2025.

notes: The text is an enrolled bill. Amended sections are reproduced in full with no marking of changed text, so new language cannot be separated from restated text. Section 45-3-7(1) exempts uses under 45-3-3 and 45-3-4 but not under 45-3-5 (publisher action). Section 45-3-2(5) defines 'generative artificial intelligence', but the operative provisions use 'personal identity', which includes AI-generated simulations (45-3-2(8)(b)). Section 6 gives the effective date as May 7, 2025.

entities.note: The text addresses 'a person' and 'an individual' generically and names no firms, facilities or public bodies. Interactive computer services are defined by reference to 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2) and are not named entities.

thresholds.note: The bill sets no numeric cutoff at which legal treatment changes. Its only number is the effective date in Section 6 (May 7, 2025), which is an event, not a threshold.
